items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: Cooper is the one who started all that... Cooper came into New York... I went in, I met Gene [Red Norvo, not Cooper].

ctx.x: Our guest tonight is Monk Hazel, who is celebrating his 50th year in jazz as a drummer, melophonist, trombone, cornet, what else? You didn't get around to any of this, huh? How has jazz drumming changed since you began, Monk?

Well, it's changed all, it's changed, it's a different thing altogether. And that, Cooper is the one who started all that. Because, you see, when we started, we were taught that the drums were supposed to be felt and not heard. And the most you ever took was a two or a four bar break. A solo, you know what you call a solo, they call them solos now. There was never no drum solos like you have today. Because if you didn't come up and did that, they'd run you off the stand.
